title: Dedicated cluster reservation tuning and QoS mitigations after capacity event
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Post-incident action ticket to address a recent dedicated cluster capacity event that caused increased latency and customer throttling. The event combined three contributors: mis-sized reservations for reserved pools, a single tenant producing large-context KV cache churn (noisy neighbor), and an overly permissive burst policy that allowed temporary oversubscription leading to evictions. This ticket coordinates short-term mitigations, medium-term platform changes, and validation criteria to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: Between 2026-02-10 03:20 UTC and 2026-02-10 04:05 UTC ~4 dedicated clusters experienced elevated queueing and a 20-40% increase in p95 token latency. Four customers on Dedicated saw degraded throughput and transient 429s from autoscaler-triggered throttles. No data loss; customer-facing SLA breaches for two enterprise tenants (incident Sev2).
root_cause: 1) Reservation sizing used historical average instead of 95th percentile peak, leaving insufficient headroom for bursts. 2) A single tenant with frequent 32k-context calls caused KV cache thrash and memory pressure, degrading co-located workloads. 3) Burst policy allowed short bursts without enforcing reservoir quotas which allowed temporary oversubscription during autoscaler scale-up lag.
detection_timeline: 2026-02-10 03:23 UTC: Alerts fired for increased scheduling latency. 03:28 UTC: Oncall identified high eviction rate on cluster-gpu-014. 03:32 UTC: Traced to tenant T-alpha producing sustained long-context sessions. 03:40 UTC: Autoscaler initiated new nodes; 03:56 UTC: Throttles and p95 latency improved as nodes registered. Postmortem held 2026-02-15.
decisions_made: 1) Immediate: apply per-tenant temporary soft-QoS to limit concurrent long-context sessions on shared clusters. 2) Medium: change reservation sizing policy to use P95 peak + 10% buffer and reserve ephemeral burst capacity separate from baseline reservations. 3) Long-term: implement tenant-aware scheduling with KV-cache-aware isolation and admission control. Approvals: infra leadership signoff on temporary QoS changes 2026-02-16; security reviewed and cleared for tenant-scoped limits 2026-02-17.
action_items: A1: Deploy temporary per-tenant soft-QoS cap (concurrent long-context sessions <= 6) for shared Dedicated clusters - owner: Liam Chen - estimate: 2 - due: 2026-02-24 - acceptance: applied to all shared clusters with dashboards showing reduced eviction rates.

A2: Update reservation-sizing algorithm to P95 + 10% buffer and add a reservation verification job - owner: Priya Rao - estimate: 3 - due: 2026-03-05 - acceptance: unit tests + historical backtest showing <5% false positive capacity deficit.

A3: Add a burst reservoir separate from steady reservations with configurable drip rate and hard cap per cluster - owner: Marco Silva - estimate: 5 - due: 2026-03-18 - acceptance: integration test and no regressions in autoscaler e2e.

A4: Implement KV-cache-aware placement filter to avoid co-locating >1 heavy KV-usage tenant per node - owner: Jen Ortega - estimate: 8 - due: 2026-04-08 - acceptance: scheduler metrics show reduced cache miss amplification.

A5: Create production chaos test (scale + noisy neighbor) in staging to validate burst policy and autoscaler recovery - owner: SRE team - estimate: 3 - due: 2026-03-01 - acceptance: run weekly with a pass/fail dashboard.

A6: Run a capacity planning review to re-evaluate reserved pool sizing for top 10 enterprise tenants - owner: Capacity Planning (Paolo Kim) - estimate: 2 - due: 2026-03-10 - acceptance: documented plan submitted to finance and sales.

A7: Add automated alerts for KV-cache thrash and per-tenant long-context rate spikes - owner: Observability (Nora Jacobs) - estimate: 2 - due: 2026-02-28 - acceptance: alerts created and tested in staging.

A8: Customer communication and remediation for affected tenants (compensation/follow-up) - owner: CSM (Ravi Desai) - estimate: 1 - due: 2026-02-20 - acceptance: support tickets closed with remediation notes.

A9: Post-deploy validation window after each change with target metric improvements and rollback playbook - owner: Deployment lead (Liam Chen) - estimate: 1 - due: ongoing - acceptance: validation report stored in Confluence.
